posts.name: Jeysie

I think it's because with Expat and KNYFE, their thing is basically ironically being gender swaps versions of very common hero archetypes that are usually male, and going with the various explorations of that switch in gender.

Whereas when you make them male, you essentially end up back with those original common hero archetypes, and it takes some of the fun out of them. Male Expat is basically the Punisher with purple hair, male KNYFE is basically just every 90s bar brawler type hero you could think of.

Whereas with Dawn, while "leader of an elite nation" (or what they see as an elite nation anyway) is also a rather common villain archetype, there's still enough variety within that archetype to work with. Male Dawn is going to still feel different from Magneto, for instance.
